review_notes: New experience supplements the original CV. Preserve earlier projects, stages, responsibilities and supplied metrics when changing emphasis between Full Stack and Frontend.

Strongwood has three distinct stages: original website April-September 2023; ERP/CRM November 2025-present; website redesign May-June 2026. Keep all three visible and do not imply uninterrupted work since 2023.

Donatella involved four months of initial development. Exact calendar dates are not confirmed; do not infer a start date from monthly billing. Subsequent maintenance and feature requests are separate from the initial development duration.

The bar app and dashboard were built for another business of the person who contracts Tomas for House of CB. Describe this within the current engagement with explicit attribution; do not present it as a House of CB product or a separate freelance contract.
English A2 is confirmed. Written work with a London-based team relies on translation tools; do not describe written or spoken English as fluent.
Henry March-August 2022 is retained from the supplied PDF; the website currently lists a different Henry end year.

The Next.js 14 migration, 30% performance improvement and 3,000+ users/hour are claims supplied in the original CV (public/assets/pdf/TomasDiBacco_Resume.pdf), retained here rather than independently measured.

Editorial review: use short action-led bullets, standard job titles and technologies in context. Omit generic claims and repeated setup details from the printed CV without changing project stages or dates. Tailor relevant, truthful keywords to each job description; do not claim an ATS score or guaranteed selection.

PostgreSQL and MySQL are listed in the published portfolio and models/data.json. They are general skills, not an assertion about the stack of Strongwood ERP or Donatella; those project stacks remain to be confirmed.
The supplied 30% performance claim is preserved; the measurement, baseline and method remain to be clarified with the author.

Additional background for future tailoring: uses AI for development and GitFlow; handled domains, Cloudflare and email setup for both freelance clients. Generic tool/practice claims and repeated setup lists are omitted where they add little to the printed narrative.
